newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi seeks approval for hypertension drug.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi seeks approval for hypertension drug.

text.p: Sanofi and Bristol-Myers Squibb have filed regulatory applications in the United States and European Union countries for marketing approval of irbesartan, a drug used to treat hypertension, Sanofi announced in a statement on Tuesday.
Irbesartan is a compound discovered by drug company Sanofi of France and co-developed with Bristol-Myers Squibb of the United States.

Sanofi said irbesartan was shown to "be extremely well tolerated with excellent blood pressure lowering efficacy over a wide range of doses" in clinical trials involving more than 6,000 patients worldwide.
Irbesartan belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin II receptor antagonists. It is taken orally and involves a single daily dose.
Sanofi said the results of Phase III clinical development of clopidogrel, a new treatment for atherothrombosis that is also a product of Sanofi research, would be known in November.
